## Overview `MultiConnector` loads each request from the first child, in config order, that reports new matched tokens, and computes the rest locally even when a later child reported more. A wrong order fails silently; this PR logs a warning when that happens and documents the rule. Related: #54240. ## Claims - Logs a warning, once per (chosen, larger) connector pair, when a later connector reported more new tokens than the chosen one, with both counts and the number of tokens computed locally. - Documents the selection rule and the `[OffloadingConnector, NixlConnector]` ordering pitfall in `docs/features/disagg_prefill.md` and the class docstring. - No behavior change: connector selection, prompt-token counters and greedy outputs are identical to main in both connector orders. ## Validation **Setup.** One prefill and one decode instance, one B300 GPU each, running `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` with `--max-model-len 16384 --enable-prefix-caching`: - **Image:** `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (0.32.1rc1.dev197+g8e2beaa3b), whose `multi_connector.py` is identical to main at 9d61ade. The "this PR" rows bind-mount this PR's file. - **Connectors:** P runs `NixlConnector` (`kv_producer`). D runs `MultiConnector` with `OffloadingConnector` (8 GB of CPU memory) and `NixlConnector` (`kv_consumer`), in the order given in the table. - **Proxy:** `tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/toy_proxy_server.py`. - **Prompts:** 8 requests sent one at a time, each a 2,048-token shared prefix followed by a unique 6,145-token body of random common English words with fixed seeds, with 32 greedy output tokens. - **Making the CPU tier hold more than GPU memory:** D first serves one request with the same prefix, so its CPU tier holds the prefix. Before each measured request, `POST /reset_prefix_cache` on D drops its GPU prefix cache and keeps the CPU tier. This stands in for GPU eviction under memory pressure. | D connector order | Code | Prompt tokens computed on D | Prompt tokens loaded on D | NIXL transfers | TTFT median, requests 2-8 | Warnings | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | `[Offloading, Nixl]` | main | 49,160 (6,145 per request) | 16,384 (CPU tier, 2,048 per request) | 0 | 0.203 s | 0 | | `[Offloading, Nixl]` | this PR | 49,160 | 16,384 | 0 | 0.206 s | 1 | | `[Nixl, Offloading]` | main | 0 | 65,544 (NIXL) | 8 | 0.138 s | 0 | | `[Nixl, Offloading]` | this PR | 0 | 65,544 | 8 | 0.141 s | 0 | - **Token counts** are deltas of `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source` on D over the 8 requests. - **P was unaffected.** It computed the same 51,208 prompt tokens in all four runs, and its `vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc` returned to 0, so P released its blocks even when D did not pull them. - **TTFT.** The first request with NIXL first (0.9-1.3 s) includes the one-time NIXL handshake, which is why the table uses requests 2-8. - **Greedy outputs.** They are identical between main and this PR in both orders (8/8). With `[Offloading, Nixl]` they also match a single instance without connectors (8/8). With `[Nixl, Offloading]`, 6 of 8 diverge from the single instance at output token 2-5, identically on main and this PR and across reruns, so this comes from the P/D path, not from this change. Warning from the second row: ``` MultiConnector loads request from connector 0 (OffloadingConnector), the first one reporting a hit, with 2048 new tokens, although connector 1 (NixlPullConnector) reported 8193. Only one connector loads a request, so the remaining 6145 tokens are computed locally. If this is not intended, list the connector expected to cover the most tokens first. Logged once per connector pair. ``` **Tests and checks:** - `pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py` in the nightly image with this change: 35 passed, 1 failed. - The new tests `test_first_hit_warns_once_when_later_connector_reports_more` and `test_first_hit_does_not_warn_without_a_larger_later_hit` (3 cases) pass. - The failure, `test_multi_connector_mixed_hma_disables_hybrid_kv_cache`, also fails without this change: it imports `test_nixl_connector.py`, which needs `ray`, and the image has no `ray`. - `test_multi_example_connector_consistency` ran with the public mirror `unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`, which has the same weights and tokenizer, because I have no access to the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`. It passes. - `pre-commit run --files ` (ruff, mypy, typos, markdownlint and the rest) passes.
Reproduction scripts: run.sh and client.py ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash # usage: MC_FILE=/path/to/multi_connector.py VLLM_REPO=/path/to/vllm bash run.sh NAME offload_first|nixl_first # Needs 2 GPUs and Qwen/Qwen3-8B in the local Hugging Face cache (the containers run offline). set -euo pipefail NAME=$1 ORDER=$2 IMAGE=${IMAGE:-vllm/vllm-openai:nightly} MODEL=${MODEL:-Qwen/Qwen3-8B} HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd) OUT=$HERE/runs/$NAME SITE=/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/multi_connector.py mkdir -p "$OUT" OFF='{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":8000000000}}' NIXL='{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer"}' P_KVT='{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer"}' if [[ $ORDER == offload_first ]]; then CONNS="[$OFF,$NIXL]"; else CONNS="[$NIXL,$OFF]"; fi D_KVT="{\"kv_connector\":\"MultiConnector\",\"kv_role\":\"kv_both\",\"kv_connector_extra_config\":{\"connectors\":$CONNS}}" cleanup() { for c in repro-p repro-d repro-proxy; do docker rm -f $c >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; done; } cleanup # Both containers see both GPUs (CUDA IPC between them); CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES order puts P on 0 and D on 1. COMMON=(--gpus all --ipc=host --pid=host --network host --shm-size 16g --ulimit memlock=-1 -v "${HF_HOME_HOST:-$HOME/.cache/huggingface}:/root/.cache/huggingface" -v "${MC_FILE:?multi_connector.py to test}:$SITE:ro" -e UCX_TLS=cuda_ipc,cuda_copy,sm,tcp -e VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST=127.0.0.1 -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1) SERVE=(--max-model-len 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 --enable-prefix-caching --max-num-seqs 16) docker run -d --name repro-p "${COMMON[@]}" -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 -e VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5600 \ "$IMAGE" "$MODEL" --port 8100 "${SERVE[@]}" --kv-transfer-config "$P_KVT" >/dev/null docker run -d --name repro-d "${COMMON[@]}" -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,0 -e VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5700 \ -e VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 "$IMAGE" "$MODEL" --port 8200 "${SERVE[@]}" --kv-transfer-config "$D_KVT" >/dev/null docker run -d --name repro-proxy --network host --entrypoint python3 \ -v "${VLLM_REPO:?path to a vllm checkout}/tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/toy_proxy_server.py:/proxy.py:ro" \ "$IMAGE" /proxy.py --port 8000 --prefiller-hosts 127.0.0.1 --prefiller-ports 8100 \ --decoder-hosts 127.0.0.1 --decoder-ports 8200 >/dev/null for port in 8100 8200; do for _ in $(seq 180); do curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:$port/health" >/dev/null && break sleep 5 done curl -sf "http://127.0.0.1:$port/health" >/dev/null || { echo "server on $port not ready"; cleanup; exit 1; } done sleep 5 python3 "$HERE/client.py" --model "$MODEL" --out "$OUT/summary.json" | tee "$OUT/client.log" for c in p d proxy; do docker logs repro-$c > "$OUT/$c.log" 2>&1 || true; done grep -h "MultiConnector loads" "$OUT/d.log" > "$OUT/multiconnector_warnings.txt" || true cleanup ``` ```python """Repro client for MultiConnector load selection (public model, synthetic text). 1. D computes one request that starts with the shared prefix S, so D's CPU tier (OffloadingConnector) stores S. 2. For each test request: reset D's GPU prefix cache (CPU tier kept), then send S + unique body through the P/D proxy. This sets up "the CPU tier holds a longer prefix than HBM", which HBM pressure produces naturally. 3. Report per-request TTFT, outputs, and the deltas of the prompt-token source counters on D and P. """ import argparse import hashlib import json import random import time import urllib.request WORDS = ( "time year people way day man thing woman life child world school state family " "student group country problem hand part place case week company system program " "question work government number night point home water room mother area money " "story fact month lot right study book eye job word business issue side kind head " "house service friend father power hour game line end member law car city name " "team minute idea body information back parent face level office door health " "person art war history party result change morning reason research girl moment " "air teacher force education river table window garden market letter music paper" ).split() def text(seed: int, n_words: int) -> str: r = random.Random(seed) return " ".join(r.choice(WORDS) for _ in range(n_words)) def post(url: str, body: dict | None = None, timeout: float = 600) -> dict: data = json.dumps(body or {}).encode() req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as r: raw = r.read() return json.loads(raw) if raw.strip() else {} def metrics(port: int) -> dict[str, float]: with urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/metrics", timeout=30) as r: out: dict[str, float] = {} for line in r.read().decode().splitlines(): if line.startswith("#") or not line.strip(): continue name, _, value = line.rpartition(" ") if "_bucket" in name or "_created" in name: continue name = name.split("{")[0] + ("{" + name.split("source=")[1].split(",")[0].rstrip("}") + "}" if "source=" in name else "") if any(k in name for k in ("prompt_tokens_by_source", "nixl", "kv_offload_total", "num_preemptions", "kv_cache_usage", "num_requests_running", "num_requests_waiting")): out[name] = out.get(name, 0.0) + float(value) return out def reset_gpu_prefix_cache(port: int) -> int: # Fails while blocks are held (e.g. in-flight CPU offload stores); retry. for attempt in range(1, 101): if post(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/reset_prefix_cache").get("success"): return attempt time.sleep(0.1) raise RuntimeError("reset_prefix_cache kept failing") def is_gauge(name: str) -> bool: return "kv_cache_usage" in name or "num_requests_" in name def delta(a: dict, b: dict) -> dict: return {k: round(b[k] - a.get(k, 0.0), 3) for k in sorted(b) if b[k] - a.get(k, 0.0)} def stream_completion(port: int, model: str, prompt: str, max_tokens: int) -> tuple[float, float, str]: body = {"model": model, "prompt": prompt, "max_tokens": max_tokens, "temperature": 0, "stream": True} req = urllib.request.Request(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/v1/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) t0 = time.perf_counter() ttft, pieces = None, [] with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=600) as r: for raw in r: line = raw.decode().strip() if not line.startswith("data:") or line == "data: [DONE]": continue chunk = json.loads(line[5:]) piece = chunk["choices"][0].get("text", "") if chunk.get("choices") else "" if piece and ttft is None: ttft = time.perf_counter() - t0 pieces.append(piece) return ttft or float("nan"), time.perf_counter() - t0, "".join(pieces) def main() -> None: ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--model", required=True) ap.add_argument("--proxy-port", type=int, default=8000) ap.add_argument("--p-port", type=int, default=8100) ap.add_argument("--d-port", type=int, default=8200) ap.add_argument("--prefix-words", type=int, default=2048) ap.add_argument("--body-words", type=int, default=6144) ap.add_argument("--requests", type=int, default=8) ap.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=32) ap.add_argument("--out", required=True) args = ap.parse_args() prefix = text(0, args.prefix_words) prompts = [prefix + "\n\n" + text(1000 + i, args.body_words) for i in range(args.requests)] tok = lambda s: len(post(f"http://127.0.0.1:{args.p_port}/tokenize", {"model": args.model, "prompt": s})["tokens"]) prefix_tokens, prompt_tokens = tok(prefix), [tok(p) for p in prompts] post(f"http://127.0.0.1:{args.d_port}/v1/completions", {"model": args.model, "prompt": prefix + "\n\n" + text(999, args.body_words), "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0}) time.sleep(3) d0, p0 = metrics(args.d_port), metrics(args.p_port) rows = [] for i, prompt in enumerate(prompts): attempts = reset_gpu_prefix_cache(args.d_port) ttft, e2e, out = stream_completion(args.proxy_port, args.model, prompt, args.max_tokens) rows.append({"i": i, "prompt_tokens": prompt_tokens[i], "ttft_s": round(ttft, 4), "e2e_s": round(e2e, 4), "reset_attempts": attempts, "output_sha1": hashlib.sha1(out.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]}) print(json.dumps(rows[-1]), flush=True) time.sleep(2) d1, p1 = metrics(args.d_port), metrics(args.p_port) ttfts = sorted(r["ttft_s"] for r in rows) summary = { "prefix_tokens": prefix_tokens, "mean_prompt_tokens": sum(prompt_tokens) / len(prompt_tokens), "ttft_mean_s": round(sum(ttfts) / len(ttfts), 4), "ttft_median_s": ttfts[len(ttfts) // 2], "d_delta": {k: v for k, v in delta(d0, d1).items() if not is_gauge(k)}, "p_delta": {k: v for k, v in delta(p0, p1).items() if not is_gauge(k)}, "d_gauges_after": {k: v for k, v in d1.items() if is_gauge(k)}, "p_gauges_after": {k: v for k, v in p1.items() if is_gauge(k)}, "rows": rows, } with open(args.out, "w") as f: json.dump(summary, f, indent=1) print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in summary.items() if k != "rows"}, indent=1)) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
## Details **How it happens.** On a decode instance with `[OffloadingConnector, NixlConnector]`: 1. GPU memory evicts part of a shared prefix, such as a system prompt. Blocks are freed tail first, so the tail goes first. 2. The CPU tier still holds that part, so `OffloadingConnector` reports a hit of a few blocks for the next request that P has already prefilled. 3. Being first in the list, it claims the request. `NixlConnector` is never asked to transfer, and D recomputes the rest of the prompt. 4. Nothing is logged. We hit this in a P/D deployment and found it only through the prompt-token counters. **Not a duplicate of #54240.** That PR adds an opt-in `range_aware` load policy so that several connectors can each load a range of the prompt. It keeps first-hit as the default, so this warning and the docs still apply with it. I found no other open PR that changes MultiConnector's load selection. **Design.** The selection logic is unchanged; the warning only reads the counts that `get_num_new_matched_tokens` already collects. It is logged once per connector pair to keep logs quiet under load. **Limitations:** - The warning compares token counts only. Preferring an earlier, faster connector that covers fewer tokens can be intentional, hence "if this is not intended". - It shows that the situation occurred, not how often; `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source` shows how often. - The reproduction forces the eviction with `/reset_prefix_cache`. How often it happens under real memory pressure depends on the workload. AI assistance (Claude, in Cursor) was used for the change, tests, reproduction and this description; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and the reproduction. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
**BEFORE SUBMITTING, PLEASE READ ** (anything written below this line will be removed by GitHub Actions)

""" import argparse import hashlib import json import random import time import urllib.request WORDS = ( "time year people way day man thing woman life child world school state family " "student group country problem hand part place case week company system program " "question work government number night point home water room mother area money " "story fact month lot right study book eye job word business issue side kind head " "house service friend father power hour game line end member law car city name " "team minute idea body information back parent face level office door health " "person art war history party result change morning reason research girl moment " "air teacher force education river table window garden market letter music paper" ).split() def text(seed: int, n_words: int) -> str: r = random.Random(seed) return " ".join(r.choice(WORDS) for _ in range(n_words)) def post(url: str, body: dict | None = None, timeout: float = 600) -> dict: data = json.dumps(body or {}).encode() req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as r: raw = r.read() return json.loads(raw) if raw.strip() else {} def metrics(port: int) -> dict[str, float]: with urllib.request.urlopen(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/metrics", timeout=30) as r: out: dict[str, float] = {} for line in r.read().decode().splitlines(): if line.startswith("#") or not line.strip(): continue name, _, value = line.rpartition(" ") if "_bucket" in name or "_created" in name: continue name = name.split("{")[0] + ("{" + name.split("source=")[1].split(",")[0].rstrip("}") + "}" if "source=" in name else "") if any(k in name for k in ("prompt_tokens_by_source", "nixl", "kv_offload_total", "num_preemptions", "kv_cache_usage", "num_requests_running", "num_requests_waiting")): out[name] = out.get(name, 0.0) + float(value) return out def reset_gpu_prefix_cache(port: int) -> int: # Fails while blocks are held (e.g. in-flight CPU offload stores); retry. for attempt in range(1, 101): if post(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/reset_prefix_cache").get("success"): return attempt time.sleep(0.1) raise RuntimeError("reset_prefix_cache kept failing") def is_gauge(name: str) -> bool: return "kv_cache_usage" in name or "num_requests_" in name def delta(a: dict, b: dict) -> dict: return {k: round(b[k] - a.get(k, 0.0), 3) for k in sorted(b) if b[k] - a.get(k, 0.0)} def stream_completion(port: int, model: str, prompt: str, max_tokens: int) -> tuple[float, float, str]: body = {"model": model, "prompt": prompt, "max_tokens": max_tokens, "temperature": 0, "stream": True} req = urllib.request.Request(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/v1/completions", data=json.dumps(body).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}) t0 = time.perf_counter() ttft, pieces = None, [] with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=600) as r: for raw in r: line = raw.decode().strip() if not line.startswith("data:") or line == "data: [DONE]": continue chunk = json.loads(line[5:]) piece = chunk["choices"][0].get("text", "") if chunk.get("choices") else "" if piece and ttft is None: ttft = time.perf_counter() - t0 pieces.append(piece) return ttft or float("nan"), time.perf_counter() - t0, "".join(pieces) def main() -> None: ap = argparse.ArgumentParser() ap.add_argument("--model", required=True) ap.add_argument("--proxy-port", type=int, default=8000) ap.add_argument("--p-port", type=int, default=8100) ap.add_argument("--d-port", type=int, default=8200) ap.add_argument("--prefix-words", type=int, default=2048) ap.add_argument("--body-words", type=int, default=6144) ap.add_argument("--requests", type=int, default=8) ap.add_argument("--max-tokens", type=int, default=32) ap.add_argument("--out", required=True) args = ap.parse_args() prefix = text(0, args.prefix_words) prompts = [prefix + "\n\n" + text(1000 + i, args.body_words) for i in range(args.requests)] tok = lambda s: len(post(f"http://127.0.0.1:{args.p_port}/tokenize", {"model": args.model, "prompt": s})["tokens"]) prefix_tokens, prompt_tokens = tok(prefix), [tok(p) for p in prompts] post(f"http://127.0.0.1:{args.d_port}/v1/completions", {"model": args.model, "prompt": prefix + "\n\n" + text(999, args.body_words), "max_tokens": 1, "temperature": 0}) time.sleep(3) d0, p0 = metrics(args.d_port), metrics(args.p_port) rows = [] for i, prompt in enumerate(prompts): attempts = reset_gpu_prefix_cache(args.d_port) ttft, e2e, out = stream_completion(args.proxy_port, args.model, prompt, args.max_tokens) rows.append({"i": i, "prompt_tokens": prompt_tokens[i], "ttft_s": round(ttft, 4), "e2e_s": round(e2e, 4), "reset_attempts": attempts, "output_sha1": hashlib.sha1(out.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]}) print(json.dumps(rows[-1]), flush=True) time.sleep(2) d1, p1 = metrics(args.d_port), metrics(args.p_port) ttfts = sorted(r["ttft_s"] for r in rows) summary = { "prefix_tokens": prefix_tokens, "mean_prompt_tokens": sum(prompt_tokens) / len(prompt_tokens), "ttft_mean_s": round(sum(ttfts) / len(ttfts), 4), "ttft_median_s": ttfts[len(ttfts) // 2], "d_delta": {k: v for k, v in delta(d0, d1).items() if not is_gauge(k)}, "p_delta": {k: v for k, v in delta(p0, p1).items() if not is_gauge(k)}, "d_gauges_after": {k: v for k, v in d1.items() if is_gauge(k)}, "p_gauges_after": {k: v for k, v in p1.items() if is_gauge(k)}, "rows": rows, } with open(args.out, "w") as f: json.dump(summary, f, indent=1) print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in summary.items() if k != "rows"}, indent=1)) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```
## Details **How it happens.** On a decode instance with `[OffloadingConnector, NixlConnector]`: 1. GPU memory evicts part of a shared prefix, such as a system prompt. Blocks are freed tail first, so the tail goes first. 2. The CPU tier still holds that part, so `OffloadingConnector` reports a hit of a few blocks for the next request that P has already prefilled. 3. Being first in the list, it claims the request. `NixlConnector` is never asked to transfer, and D recomputes the rest of the prompt. 4. Nothing is logged. We hit this in a P/D deployment and found it only through the prompt-token counters. **Not a duplicate of #54240.** That PR adds an opt-in `range_aware` load policy so that several connectors can each load a range of the prompt. It keeps first-hit as the default, so this warning and the docs still apply with it. I found no other open PR that changes MultiConnector's load selection. **Design.** The selection logic is unchanged; the warning only reads the counts that `get_num_new_matched_tokens` already collects. It is logged once per connector pair to keep logs quiet under load. **Limitations:** - The warning compares token counts only. Preferring an earlier, faster connector that covers fewer tokens can be intentional, hence "if this is not intended". - It shows that the situation occurred, not how often; `vllm:prompt_tokens_by_source` shows how often. - The reproduction forces the eviction with `/reset_prefix_cache`. How often it happens under real memory pressure depends on the workload. AI assistance (Claude, in Cursor) was used for the change, tests, reproduction and this description; I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and the reproduction. ---

@@ -35,6 +35,8 @@ Now supports 9 types of connectors:
   --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_both"},{"kv_connector":"ExampleConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"shared_storage_path":"local_storage"}}]}}'
   ```
 
+  KV is saved to every connector but loaded from only one per request: the first connector in the list that reports any new matched tokens. Tokens it does not cover are computed locally, even if a later connector reported them, so the order matters. For example, on a decode instance with `[OffloadingConnector, NixlConnector]`, a CPU hit on the tail of a shared prefix that was evicted from GPU memory claims the request, and the decode instance recomputes the prompt tokens that NIXL would have transferred. Listing `NixlConnector` first avoids this. MultiConnector logs a warning, once per pair of connectors, when a later connector reported more tokens than the one it picked.
+
 - **OffloadingConnector**: enable offloading of KV data to CPU memory, customizing the CPU block size (in tokens) and total CPU memory bytes to allocate:
